claims.explanation: PD-98059 is a MEK1/2 inhibitor, so selectivity is best explained by dependence on the RAF-MEK-ERK pathway. Tumors with upstream pathway activation (BRAF, KRAS, NRAS, NF1 loss, MAP2K1 mutation, EGFR/RAS-driven NSCLC) should be sensitized, while lines with alternative survival signaling through PI3K-AKT (PTEN loss, PIK3CA mutation) or other bypass mechanisms are protected. The virtual-cell signature (DUSP6/FOSL1/MYC down, CDKN1A/SESN1 up) and similarity to MEK/RAF inhibitors support on-pathway ERK suppression as the killing mechanism.

features.basis: BRAF V600/hotspot mutations activate MEK-ERK and predict MEK-inhibitor sensitivity; enriched in killed melanoma/colorectal lines
KRAS mutations drive ERK-pathway dependence; seen in killed lung, gastric, ovarian, melanoma lines
NRAS mutations activate RAF-MEK-ERK; present in killed IPC298 melanoma
NF1 loss causes RAS-ERK hyperactivation; enriched in killed melanoma, glioma, upper-aerodigestive lines
MEK1 activating mutations directly increase dependence on the drug's target; seen in killed NCIH1437
EGFR-mutant NSCLC signals through RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK; killed lines include NCIH1650 and HCC4006
DUSP6 is an ERK-pathway feedback gene strongly downregulated in the virtual-cell response, marking active ERK dependence
FOSL1/AP-1 is ERK-driven and downregulated by PD-98059 in the virtual cell, indicating MAPK-pathway addiction
MYC is downregulated in the virtual-cell response and ERK signaling supports MYC-driven proliferation
PTEN loss activates PI3K-AKT bypass survival signaling; enriched in least-affected lines (UACC62, K029AX, FTC133, ZR751)
PIK3CA mutation provides PI3K-AKT survival signaling independent of MEK; seen in least-affected MKN1, HGC27, HEC265
CDKN2A loss may reflect lines with alternative proliferation/survival wiring; enriched among least-affected lines
